A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DIFFPUTER diffusion-and-EM imputation work despite the changed title. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original imputation benchmarks and iteration/missing-rate experiments in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmarks, sampling sensitivity, runtime and EM-augmented generative-model experiments in Section 5 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: Section 4.3 replaces binary analog-bit categorical encoding and threshold decoding with one-hot encoding and argmax decoding, shown in v2 Figure 1. The diffusion objective, denoising architecture and alternating EM procedure remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: Reported coverage drops Beijing, leaving nine datasets despite residual references to ten. Out-of-sample reporting contracts from ten datasets in v1 Figure 4 to six in v2 Table 6, also omitting Magic, Bean and News. New California/Adult tests extend missingness to 99%; the underlying tabular imputation tasks remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated KNN comparisons and the Mean/Median/MF row in Table 1. TabCSDI and MissDiff join the MAR/MNAR comparisons, while MissDiff disappears from out-of-sample reporting. Table 3 substantially expands comparisons through HIWAE, VAEM, HH-VAEM and EM-augmented versions of these models and MIWAE.

E3.justification: Categorical preprocessing changes to one-hot encoding, and new experiments introduce sampling-count/step sweeps and GPU timing comparisons. The principal 70/30 split, 30% missing rate, evaluation metrics and default N=10 and M=50 remain unchanged. Newly documented baseline tuning does not establish that earlier experimental settings changed.

E4.justification: v2 retains the EM-iteration analysis but adds sensitivity to sampled imputations and diffusion steps, runtime comparisons, extreme-missingness tests and EM-with-other-generative-model controls. These address practical cost and component effectiveness absent from v1. The earlier Beijing missing-rate comparison against competing methods is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten generated masks and mean/standard-deviation reporting. However, v1 Figures 9–10 show MAR/MNAR uncertainty bars, whereas their replacements, v2 Tables 7–10, contain point estimates only. No increase in repeated runs or new significance-testing procedure is established.

E6.justification: Reported average MAE/RMSE advantages change from 8.10%/5.64% to 6.94%/4.78%; changed dataset and comparator coverage prevents interpreting this as a matched performance decline. Categorical and other benchmark results are revised, entries are removed, and substantial new sampling, runtime and EM-combination results appear.

T1.justification: The main theorem and diffusion derivations remain. In proof Equation 11, v2 changes the final Monte Carlo approximation into an equality and deletes its approximation explanation without adding a derivation. Section 4.1 also changes the likelihood-optimization interpretation from exact to approximate. The theorem's explicit limiting conditions already appeared in v1's proof.

C1.justification: The central EM–diffusion method, likelihood/EAP correspondence and superior-imputation claims remain. v2 sharpens novelty positioning: its introduction calls diffusion combined with EM unexplored, and Section 2 explicitly claims the first such integration, replacing v1's broader emphasis on underexplored deep-generative EM.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of sampling accuracy versus cost, attributes extreme-missingness behavior to mean initialization, and argues for advantages over EM-enhanced generative alternatives. It removes v1's Beijing-specific robustness interpretation and stochastic-versus-deterministic variance explanation. Some new interpretations overreach: Table 3's general improvement narrative overlooks HIWAE deterioration on three datasets.

D1.justification: New Appendix D.6 documents baseline tuning, including 12,000 MOT/TDM iterations, TabCSDI architecture/batch choices and 50-trial searches for several baselines. v2 also expands mask-generation instructions, specifies out-of-sample inference, adds supplementary-code access instructions and reports training times. These substantially expand documentation; they do not establish corresponding changes to previously executed experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds image-inpainting and heterogeneous-VAE context, including LatentPaint, VAEM and hierarchical-model references, and focuses novelty more specifically on diffusion within EM. Most existing related-work discussion remains. Citation-style changes and duplicate bibliography entries do not represent additional research coverage.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial introduction passages are rewritten, Section 4.3 is reorganized around implementation and inference, and the results discussion adopts thematic observations. Appendices are reorganized with a symbol glossary and dedicated baseline-hyperparameter section. These changes substantially revise explanation and navigation beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: The full MCAR comparison moves into the main figure, while categorical, out-of-sample and MAR/MNAR plots become tables. v2 adds sensitivity plots and runtime, EM-combination and notation tables, revises Figure 1, removes Algorithm 3 and adopts the ICLR layout. Much retained evidence is substantially redisplayed.

improvement.justification: The new sampling/runtime controls and baseline-tuning documentation make practical choices and comparisons easier to assess than in v1. The net gain is limited by reduced benchmark coverage, lost MAR/MNAR uncertainty reporting and unresolved proof/reporting problems, including the unsupported equality in Equation 11 and inconsistent improvement percentages within Table 6.
